newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish kidnap victim shot despite huge rally.
newsitem.headline: Spanish kidnap victim shot despite huge rally.

text.p: A Spanish politician abducted by Basque guerrillas was found shot in the head, barely clinging to life, on Saturday despite a rally of half a million led by the prime minister to protest at the kidnappers' threat to kill him.
Hospital officials said Miguel Angel Blanco was in "extremely serious" condition in a coma with two bullets lodged in his brain. Surgeons decided not to try to remove the bullets.
Basque separatist ETA rebels kidnapped Blanco on Thursday and threatened to kill him at 4 p.m. (1400 GMT) on Saturday if the government did not change its prison policy.
Blanco was found, with his hands tied, by a hunter who heard a shot in a wooded area near the northern Basque coastal city of San Sebastian. A man was seen running from the scene.
Police later found a bomb in a car they believed was used as a getaway car by the kidnappers.
Blanco was rushed to hospital and a duty judge who went there reported Blanco was dead. Hospital officials later said he was alive and in a coma.

The attempted killing took place despite the huge rally led by Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar in the Basque capital Bilbao, which officals said was the biggest protest against ETA separatist rebels in history.
Blanco is a young town councillor from Aznar's ruling Popular Party.
ETA kidnapped Blanco on Thursday and said they would kill him unless the government gave in to its ultimatum to move some 500 ETA inmates to prisons in the Basque country by 4 p.m. on Saturday.
The kidnapping and death threat caused outrage across Spain, which had just been celebrating the release of two other ETA hostages last week, and sparked an angry backlash.
Even nationalist politicians in the region who support the separatist cause but oppose violence turned out for the protest and called on ETA to release Blanco.

"They (ETA) have to know we cannot live with this barbarity any longer. If they carry out this threat, the Basque people will never, never forgive them," Basque interior counsellor Juan Maria Atutxa told state television in Bilbao.

Aznar headed the protest march in Bilbao marching alongside his wife and fierce Basque nationalist leader Jose Antonio Ardanza. They carried a yellow banner at the front that said "Peace Now and Forever" in the Basque language.
Some 200 neighbours of Blanco had staged an all-night vigil in the town hall and there were protests across Spain both on Friday and Saturday.

Residents in Ermua, Blanco's hometown, and thousands of supporters at a vigil that started as ETA's deadline passed, began screaming and crying when the erroneous news that he had been killed was announced.
But when word spread that he was still alive, the crowd erupted in relieved shouts of "Thank God!"
The government strongly condemned the kidnap and shooting and urged calm in the region.

"This is a terrorist band that has been condemned by all of Spain...There is no sense in what they have done. There is no justification for this kind of torment," chief government spokesman Miguel Angel Rodriguez told reporters.

ETA has killed some 800 people since starting a drive for Basque independence in 1968. The rebels have set deadlines to execute kidnap victims twice before, in 1981 and 1983, and in both cases the hostages were killed.
